subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Road safety: discussion, vocabulary and multiple-choice strategy
outcomes: Talk about road safety and the work of the Traffic Safety Institute
Learn road safety words such as fatalities and simulator
Use a strategy to answer multiple-choice listening questions

tf.s: The simulator car shows people why wearing a seatbelt is important.
tf.why: Yes, it lets people feel why a seatbelt matters.

tf.s: 'Fatalities' are people who are killed in accidents.
In 2014 there were 836 road accidents in Oman.
tf.why: 836 was the number of fatalities; there were 6,717 accidents.

tf.s: Qualifying words like 'always' and 'never' can make a correct-looking answer wrong.
tf.why: Right, one small word can change the whole meaning.

tf.s: In multiple-choice questions, it helps to cross out the options you know are wrong.
tf.why: Yes, eliminating wrong options leaves you with the best answer.

tf.s: The ROP advises new drivers to practise driving at the busiest times of day.
tf.why: The advice is to avoid busy times while you are still new.

tf.s: Driving without a licence can lead to a fine and time in jail.
tf.why: Correct, the fine is 75 rials and at least 48 hours in jail.

tf.s: A speed limit is the lowest speed you are allowed to drive on a road.
tf.why: A speed limit is the highest speed allowed.

tf.s: The ROP suggests that new drivers go out with an experienced driver.
tf.why: Yes, an experienced driver can help a new driver stay safe.

tf.s: You should read the multiple-choice options only after the talk has finished.
tf.why: It is best to read the statements before you listen.

boxes.why: Fatalities are people who die, for example in accidents.

boxes.why: It lets people feel what happens without a seatbelt.

boxes.q: How many road accidents were there in Oman in 2014?

boxes.why: Words like sometimes, never and always qualify a statement.

boxes.q: Who gave the talk in Listening 4.3.1?
boxes.why: An officer from the ROP talked about road safety.

boxes.q: What should you do first in a multiple-choice listening task?
boxes.why: Reading first tells you what to listen for.

boxes.why: A seatbelt holds you safely in your seat.

boxes.why: The minimum is 48 hours in jail.

mcq.q: What does the Traffic Safety Institute teach people about?
mcq.why: The institute teaches people how to be safe on the roads.
Fatalities is the word for people who are killed.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of the simulator car?
o: to show the importance of wearing a seatbelt
mcq.why: The simulator lets people feel the effect of a crash safely.

mcq.q: Which is NOT advice the ROP gives to new drivers?
o: go out with an experienced driver
mcq.why: Speeding is never good advice; the other three are from the talk.

mcq.q: A statement says: 'New drivers should never drive alone.' Which word could make it wrong?
mcq.why: Qualifying words like never can turn a statement false.

mcq.q: You are not sure of an answer. Two options are clearly wrong. What should you do?
o: eliminate them and choose from the rest
mcq.why: Eliminating wrong options improves your chance of being right.

mcq.q: A man drives with no licence. What can happen to him?
o: a 75-rial fine and at least 48 hours in jail
mcq.why: The talk gives both a fine and jail time.

mcq.q: In 2014, 6,717 accidents caused 836 deaths. What does this show?
o: road accidents are a serious problem
roads in Oman are always safe
most accidents cause no harm to anyone
there were more deaths than accidents
mcq.why: Hundreds of deaths show why road safety matters so much.

mcq.q: Why do qualifying words matter in multiple-choice questions?
o: they can make an otherwise correct answer incorrect
they are never in exam questions
mcq.why: One word like always or never can change the meaning.

mcq.q: Why is it good for a new driver to go out with an experienced driver?
o: the experienced driver can guide and correct them
it makes the car go faster
they can drive without a licence
it lets them use busy roads at night
mcq.why: Learning from someone with experience makes new drivers safer.
